research_question: Hvordan fordeles musikalsk handlingsrom og teknisk risiko mellom kropp, sensor, mapping, programvare og lydsyntese i digitale instrumenter?

bibliographic_identity.title: The Obstacle Course of DMI Performance: Two Case Studies with T-Stick and Karlax
bibliographic_identity.publication: Proceedings of the International Conference on New Interfaces for Musical Expression 2024

production_source_extensions.registration_reason: Open peer-reviewed case comparison that traces two performance systems through physical controllers, mappings, software dependencies and performance preparation.

locators.supports: The case traces sensor data through Max and Webmapper and identifies dependencies in the mapping and software chain.
The authors compare the two performance systems and distinguish technical, mapping, rehearsal and obsolescence obstacles.

claim_records.statement: Moriceau og medforfatteres T-Stick- og Karlax-case viser at et digitalt instruments handlingsrom ikke sitter i kontrolleren alene: sensorstrøm, Max-patch, Webmapper eller annen mapping, lydmotor, programvareversjon og innøvd repertoar danner én framføringskjede, og blant annet Libmapper-obsolesens blir derfor et musikalsk så vel som teknisk hinder; sammenligningen dokumenterer to systemforløp, ikke en universell rangering av digitale instrumenter.
locators: Moriceau et al. 2024, PDF Sections 2–3 and Figure 4: T-Stick sensing, Max and Webmapper mapping layers
Moriceau et al. 2024, PDF Sections 4–5: Karlax case, software dependencies and cross-case obstacle synthesis
